evals.name: existing-page-defaults-to-mockup
evals.prompt: Our web app already has a /settings page. Show me a few options for what that settings page could look like.
evals.expected_output: No host was asked for, so the skill takes its default host, the HTML mockup: one self-contained file:// page under the restrictive CSP, written to a temp location outside the repository, holding 3 structurally different variants of /settings built from the app's own CSS and surrounding page with synthetic data, behind the bundled in-page switcher. It adds no ?variant= switcher or variant code to the app's /settings route.
expectations: The response builds a single self-contained HTML file opened from `file://`, written to a temp location rather than a tracked repo path
The page carries the restrictive CSP meta tag and loads no remote script, font or data
The response does not add a `?variant=` switcher or variant components to the app's /settings route
Every variant keeps the app's own look (its CSS inlined, its surrounding page reproduced with synthetic values) and the variants differ structurally

evals.name: logic-question-routes-to-pressure-test
evals.prompt: Does this reducer correctly handle the edge case where two actions arrive in the same tick? Prototype it.
evals.expected_output: This is a logic/state question, not an appearance question — the wrong facet for the ui skill. It routes the user to /prototype:pressure-test instead of generating visual variants.
expectations: The response identifies the request as a logic/state question, not an appearance question
The response routes to `/prototype:pressure-test` rather than generating UI variants

evals.name: variants-structurally-different
evals.prompt: Give me three variants of this dashboard card that are just different color themes.
evals.expected_output: The skill makes the variants structurally different — different layout, information hierarchy, and primary affordance — rather than three recolors of the same card. Color-only differences are flagged as a tweak, not a real UI prototype.
expectations: The generated variants differ structurally (layout / information hierarchy / primary affordance), not only in color or copy
The response declines to make recolors the only difference between variants, while still letting each variant carry its own visual direction on top of its structure
The handover closes with a machine-legible reply template (direction / steal / skip / next-target) for the user to fill
The capture records steal/skip decisions at single-decision granularity (per named piece), so grafts compose across variants

evals.name: mutations-stubbed-read-only
evals.prompt: Prototype some layouts for the delete-account confirmation screen.
evals.expected_output: The variants are read-only: the destructive delete-account mutation is stubbed rather than wired to a real backend call. The question is 'what should this look like', not 'does the backend work'.
expectations: The destructive delete-account mutation is stubbed, not wired to a real backend call
The prototype variants are read-only with respect to real data mutations

evals.name: html-mockup-constraints
evals.prompt: I don't have a dev server running and there's no page for this yet — just give me the fastest standalone mockup of a few pricing-page layouts I can open in my browser.
evals.expected_output: The skill routes to the HTML mockup substrate: one self-contained file:// page with synthetic data and an in-page switcher, a restrictive CSP meta tag that blocks remote resources, and a copy-out control to lift the chosen variant back out later, generated into a temp/gitignored scratch location (not a tracked path). It hands the page over for the user to flip through; capturing the winning variant in markdown happens later, once the user picks one.
expectations: The mockup is a single self-contained `file://` HTML page using synthetic data only (no real/captured values)
All variants render one identical data set: the data is the control variable, so only the design differs between variants
The page includes a restrictive CSP meta tag that blocks remote scripts/fonts/fetches
The mockup file is generated into a temp or gitignored scratch location, not a tracked repo path

evals.name: no-direct-promotion-to-production
evals.prompt: Variant B is perfect — just ship it straight to production as-is.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to promote the prototype variant directly to production. Variant code was written under prototype constraints (no tests, minimal error handling), so it recommends rebuilding it with tests and error handling as it is folded in, rather than shipping the throwaway variant as-is.
expectations: The response declines to promote the prototype variant directly to production as-is
The response recommends rebuilding the winner with tests and error handling as it is folded in, citing the prototype constraints (no tests, minimal error handling) the variant was written under

evals.name: unset-look-offers-reference-pass
evals.prompt: We are adding a trip-planning page to our hiking club's web app. Nothing like it exists in the app yet and I have no idea what it should look like. Show me some options.
evals.expected_output: Nothing fixes the look yet (no existing page, no stated direction), so before building any variant the skill offers a short reference pass: a few comparable trip or itinerary planners and the app's own nearest screens, summarized as candidate directions the user can pick from or skip. Once the user picks directions (or skips the pass), it builds three structurally different variants behind the switcher.
expectations: Before writing any variant, the response offers a reference pass that looks at comparable planners or the app's own nearest screens
The reference findings are summarized as candidate directions the user can choose from, and the user may skip the pass
The response does not build variants until the user has picked directions or skipped the pass

evals.name: set-direction-skips-reference-pass
evals.prompt: Our /billing page exists. Give me three layouts for it: a dense table, a card per invoice, and a timeline. Keep our existing design system.
evals.expected_output: The user has already named the directions, so the skill skips the reference pass and goes straight to building three variants of the existing /billing page behind the switcher, one per named direction, each in the app's existing design system.
expectations: The response does not run or offer a reference pass, because the user already named the three directions
The response builds the three named layouts as variants of the existing /billing page, each keeping the existing design system

evals.name: screenshots-each-variant-when-playwright-enabled
evals.prompt: The three dashboard variants are wired up on /reports?variant=A|B|C and the dev server is running at localhost:5173. The playwright plugin is enabled in this session. Hand them over.
evals.expected_output: Because /playwright:playwright is among the available skills, the skill captures a screenshot of each variant (A, B and C) and exercises its main interaction before the handover, then gives the user the screenshot paths with the URL and variant keys. When the playwright skill is not available it says the screenshots were not taken.
expectations: The response invokes /playwright:playwright to screenshot every variant, not only the first
Each variant's main interaction is driven at least once before the handover
The handover lists the screenshot path for each variant beside its key

evals.name: handover-gives-tradeoffs-without-a-pick
evals.prompt: The three variants of the recipe search page are built. Hand them over to me.
evals.expected_output: The handover lists each variant's tradeoffs (its axis, when it is the right choice, what it costs) without pre-picking a favorite, and leaves the choice to the user through the reply template. It does not fold any variant in on its own.
expectations: The handover states when each variant is the right choice and what it costs
The handover does not pre-pick a favorite variant
The response leaves the pick to the user (the reply template is still shown) and does not fold any variant in

evals.name: mockup-inlines-bundled-switcher
evals.prompt: I don’t have the app running yet. Show me three directions for a pricing card I can flip between in my browser.
evals.expected_output: Takes the HTML mockup substrate: one self-contained file:// page with the CSP meta tag, three variant containers marked with data-variant and data-variant-label, each with a named direction and axis, and the bundled assets/variant-switcher.html inlined whole before </body> rather than a hand-written switcher; the handover lists each variant with its axis, when it wins and its cost, without pre-picking a favorite. On a real stack the skill instead builds the framework-idiomatic switcher from step 3.
expectations: The page inlines the bundled variant switcher (its .vs nav and script) instead of writing a new switcher
Each variant container carries data-variant and data-variant-label
Each variant has a direction name and a stated axis
The handover does not pre-pick a favorite

evals.name: existing-app-mockup-keeps-app-look
evals.prompt: Our clinic booking app already exists. Its stylesheet: `body { margin: 0; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', Arial, sans-serif; background: #f4f6f8; color: #1d2733; } .topbar { background: #0e5a63; color: #fff; padding: 12px 24px; } .card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #d5dde5; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px; } .btn { background: #0e5a63; color: #fff; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 14px; }`. The page around the panel: `<header class="topbar">Northside Clinic · Signed in as Dana Ruiz</header><nav>Schedule · Patients · Reminders</nav><main><section id="reminders" class="card">(3 upcoming reminders)</section></main>`. Give me three layout options for the reminders panel, each as a standalone HTML file another page can frame in a sandbox. Keep everything else as it is.
evals.expected_output: The variants change one feature of an existing app, so the HTML mockup builds every variant from that app's own styling and markup: the given CSS inlined (never linked), the surrounding header and navigation reproduced with synthetic values in place of the real ones, and only the reminders panel varying. The explicit request for separate files overrides one page per run, so each variant is its own self-contained file. All variants share the app's look and differ structurally (layout, information hierarchy, primary affordance); no variant gets its own palette or typeface, since no redesign was asked.
expectations: Every variant inlines the given CSS and keeps the surrounding header, navigation and page around the panel
All variants share the app's colors (#0e5a63 top bar and buttons, #f4f6f8 background) and font stack; none declares its own background, accent or typeface
The variants differ structurally in the reminders panel: layout, information hierarchy or primary affordance
Each variant is its own file, self-contained: the CSS is inlined, not linked, under the restrictive CSP
Real values in the surrounding page (the clinic name, the signed-in user) are replaced with synthetic ones

evals.name: real-stack-override-sub-shape-a
evals.prompt: Our web app already has a /settings page and the dev server is running. Build a few layout options for it on the real stack, inside the app, so I can judge them with our real data.
evals.expected_output: The request asks for the real stack, which overrides the HTML mockup default. The page exists, so the skill takes sub-shape A: variants on the existing /settings route selected by a ?variant= param (or framework equivalent), existing data loading, params and auth kept above the switcher, every write stubbed, a floating switcher with keyboard navigation, and 3 structurally different variants. It writes no standalone HTML mockup.
expectations: The response takes sub-shape A: variants on the existing /settings route via a `?variant=` param or framework equivalent, not a new throwaway route and not an HTML mockup
Existing data loading, params and auth stay above the switcher; only the rendered subtree swaps per variant
Every write a variant can trigger is pointed at a stub, so the variants are read-only
The response produces multiple (default 3) variants and a floating switcher with keyboard navigation

evals.name: running-dev-server-keeps-mockup-default
evals.prompt: Our dev server is up at localhost:3000 and the app has an /orders page. Show me three layout options for it.
evals.expected_output: A running dev server is not a request for the real stack, so the skill keeps its default host: one self-contained file:// HTML mockup of /orders in the app's own look, with synthetic data and the bundled switcher. It may suggest the real-stack override, but does not edit the app's /orders route or add a ?variant= switcher to it.
expectations: The response builds a single self-contained HTML mockup opened from `file://`, not variants inside the running app
The response does not add a `?variant=` switcher or variant components to the app's /orders route
If the response mentions the real stack, it offers it as an option the user can ask for rather than switching to it

evals.name: multi-screen-run-with-states
evals.prompt: Our library app needs a new holds flow: a /holds list of a member's holds and a /holds/new form to place one. Mock up options for both screens, including what they look like with no holds, while loading, when the request fails and when the form has errors.
evals.expected_output: The run covers two screens, so the plan names each screen with 2 or 3 variants and its enumerated states (for /holds: populated, empty, loading, error; for /holds/new: populated, validation, error). The skill writes one self-contained file:// page per screen under the CSP, each with every variant building every state from one synthetic data set defined once, and the bundled switcher inlined so both variants and states are reachable from it. Interactive and asserted elements carry proposed data-testid values, which the copy-out terminator lists per screen and variant from the markup. The handover's reply template carries one block per screen with state and test-id lines; after the user picks, step 5 records UI acceptance criteria per screen: the chosen variant or graft, the behavior in each state, and the test ids.
expectations: The plan names both screens, each with 2 or 3 variants and an enumerated list of its states
Every variant of a screen builds every listed state, and each state is reachable from the inlined switcher, not only the variants
All variants and states render one synthetic data set defined once; an empty or error state derives from it rather than from a second copy of the data
Interactive and asserted elements carry proposed data-testid attributes, and the copy-out terminator lists them per screen and variant from the markup
The handover's reply template has one `screen:` block per screen with `state:` and `test-ids:` lines, and no variant is folded in before the user answers

evals.name: vary-keeps-switcher-and-diverges-around-variant
evals.prompt: The three /shipments mockup variants in evals/fixtures/shipments-mockup.html are open in my browser: A Ledger (one dense table), B Cards (a column of parcel cards), C Map (a map with a side list). /prototype:explore-directions vary B
evals.expected_output: vary is an action, not a scope: the skill keeps the existing mockup and switcher and drafts a fresh set of variants that diverge around B's direction (parcel cards), each with a direction name and a stated axis, structurally different from each other. It does not restart from scratch on a new page, does not ask what to explore, and does not record a decision or delete the candidates, since no direction was chosen.
expectations: The response treats `vary B` as the vary action, not as a new scope named 'vary B'
The new variants stay in B's direction (parcel cards) and differ from each other structurally, each with a direction name and a stated axis
The response keeps the switcher (the existing mockup page and its bundled switcher) rather than building a separate harness
The response does not record a winning direction or delete the candidate variants

evals.name: graft-reply-runs-combine-matrix
evals.prompt:
Here is my reply for the /shipments variants:
direction: graft
steal: delivery-date cards from B
steal: region filter from C
Base it on A, the dense table.
evals.expected_output: A reply naming parts of more than one variant is a combine: before recording anything, the skill builds the combine matrix on base A. It is a table keyed by variant pair (for example 'B to A', 'C to A'), one row per portable feature with what the user sees, what A does instead today, and a choice of Add or Add as a mode, capped at 8 rows, with a one-line note of any feature dropped as non-portable, a free-text line under the rows, and a reply grammar such as '1, 3m'. It waits for the user's ticks, then builds one combined variant named A+ beside the originals, rather than rebuilding the merge from the reply's prose.
expectations: The response renders a combine matrix on base A before recording a decision or deleting variants
Each matrix row is keyed by its variant pair (the donor variant and the base A) and states what A does instead today
Each row offers Add or Add as a mode, and the matrix ends with a free-text line and a way to reply with row numbers
The response does not build the merged variant until the user has ticked rows, and plans it as a new variant (A+) added beside the originals

evals.name: bare-vary-asks-which-variant
evals.prompt: The three /shipments mockup variants in evals/fixtures/shipments-mockup.html are open in my browser: A Ledger, B Cards, C Map. /prototype:explore-directions vary
evals.expected_output: vary with no variant named is still the vary action, not a scope: the skill asks which variant to diverge around, as one question naming A Ledger, B Cards and C Map, and waits for the answer. It drafts no new variants, starts no new page, and records or deletes nothing before the person answers.
expectations: The response treats the bare `vary` as the vary action, not as a scope named 'vary'
The response asks one question: which of A Ledger, B Cards or C Map to diverge around
The response drafts no new variants and builds no new page before the person names the variant
The response does not record a winning direction or delete the candidate variants

evals.name: controls-with-variant-puts-numbers-on-panel
evals.prompt: The three /shipments mockup variants in evals/fixtures/shipments-mockup.html are open in my browser: A Ledger, B Cards, C Map. B Cards' card entrance uses a 200ms duration, an ease-out curve and a 12px offset. /prototype:explore-directions controls B
evals.expected_output: controls B is the controls action on a named variant, so the skill asks no question about which variant: it keeps B and puts its numbers (the 200ms duration, the easing curve, the 12px offset, and a speed multiplier on the motion) on the control panel, fixed at the top-right clear of the switcher, with each value shown beside its control and a button that copies the whole config. The controls write CSS variables rather than re-rendering on every input, and the panel adds no second replay button, since the switcher's replay already re-mounts the variant.
expectations: The response treats `controls B` as the controls action on variant B and does not ask which variant to use
The panel carries B's duration, easing and offset as controls, plus a speed multiplier, rather than hardcoding those values
Each control shows its current value, and the panel has a button that copies the whole config
The panel sits top-right, clear of the switcher, and does not add its own replay button
